title: introduce-cohort-emulator-with-flame-segmentation-reporter
author: Priya Natarajan
ci_status: pass (perf job rerun once due to baseline noise)
release_notes: Add a cohort emulator and flame-segmentation reporter to improve attribution of tail microbursts to kernel hotspots; includes goldset generator and example cohorts.
description: Context: We often see p95/p99 spikes in the benchmark lab but lack a compact, deterministic way to map tail episodes to kernel-level hotspots across cohorts. This PR adds a lightweight cohort emulator that replays compact multi-session cohorts with controlled timing and a new flame-segmentation reporter that emits compact 'flame segment' artifacts for downstream attribution and visualization. Motivation: Make it possible to reproduce microburst segments deterministically, compare them against a golden set, and quickly iterate on kernel/serving changes without full cluster replays. Scope: emulator core, segmentation reporter, goldset generator, CI perf job integration, docs and an example cohort. Checklist: - [x] Emulator core with deterministic seed and time dilation - [x] Flame-segmentation reporter that emits compact JSON segments and optional pprof links - [x] Goldset generator and compare tool (scripts/generate_goldset.sh) - [x] Perf CI job and threshold gating (bench/ci/perf_job.yaml) - [x] Example cohort and quickstart doc (docs/bench/cohort_emulator.md, examples/cohorts/sample_cohort.json) - [x] Unit tests and an integration perf harness (tests/integration/test_cohort_emulator.py) Limitations: This emulator is intentionally lower-fidelity than our full session replayer — it samples representative KV/cache priming and seq-length mixes rather than reproducing exact traffic. The goal is fast, repeatable reproduction of hotspot segments rather than absolute latency parity. Related: ENG-2198 (cohort diagnostics), ENG-2217 (perf regression tooling).
